sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Isanti County?
sections.html:
Two county offices split the work: the Assessor sets value and classification, and the Auditor-Treasurer bills and collects. Mail for the Assessor goes to Isanti County Assessor, 555 18th Avenue SW, Cambridge, MN 55008.

The Isanti County Assessor estimates the market value of every parcel and decides its classification under Minnesota statutes and Department of Revenue standards. The same page carries the forms for agricultural use, homestead, local option disaster abatement, managed forest and the disabled veterans market value exclusion. Cambridge is the county seat, and a seller who has a question about a bill, a classification or a payoff should start with these two counters before anyone else.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Isanti County before pricing a house?
sections.html:
Isanti County is a growing exurban county in east-central Minnesota, and the Census numbers show it. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 44,386 residents, up 7.9% from the April 2020 base of 41,128.

The county was formed on February 13, 1857, covers about 436 square miles of land, and sits inside the Minneapolis-St. Paul-Bloomington metropolitan area. The Rum River runs south through its middle. The cities are Cambridge, Isanti, Braham (partly in Kanabec County) and St. Francis (mostly in Anoka County). Anoka County borders it on the south, which is why many owners commute to the metro. Census figures put the mean trip to work at 30.7 minutes, longer than in the other three counties covered in this series.

  • Housing units: 18,068 in July 2025, with 276 building permits issued in 2025.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 83.7% for 2020 to 2024, so most sellers here are owners of long standing.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $306,200 for 2020 to 2024.
  • Median household income: $87,440, with median gross rent at $1,273.

Ask the Auditor-Treasurer for the exact figure on your parcel, because the median says nothing about your own bill.

sections.h2: Who owns homes in Isanti County, and where do they live?
sections.html:
Most Isanti County homes are lived in by their owners, and the county is split between town and country. The 2020 census counted 15,615 households and 16,550 housing units, with 5.6% of units vacant and 82.5% of occupied units owner-occupied.

Wikipedia's county summary adds that 40.7% of residents lived in urban areas and 59.3% in rural areas, with a median age of 39.6. The terrain is hilly, cut by gullies and dotted with lakes and ponds, and the highest point is near the northwest corner at about 1,020 feet. Neighbors are Kanabec, Pine, Chisago, Anoka, Sherburne and Mille Lacs counties.

  • Small parks and wildlife areas include Maywood County Park, Springvale County Park and the Twin Lake Scientific and Natural Area.
  • Rural parcels can sit in agricultural, managed forest or Green Acres programs, each with its own application date on the county calendar.
  • Agricultural use has to be in place by January 2 of the assessment year to count for the following payable year.

For a seller, the rural and urban mix matters because the assessor's classification of the parcel feeds directly into the tax calculation.

sections.h2: When are Isanti County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Most residential and agricultural owners pay the first half by May 15 and the second half by October 15, with agricultural second halves moving to November 15. Manufactured homes follow a different calendar.

Isanti County property tax due dates by classification
Due dateWhat is due
May 15First half, residential and agricultural
August 31First half, manufactured homes (whole bill if $50 or less)
October 15Second half, residential only
November 15Second half, manufactured homes and agricultural

Source: Isanti County Auditor-Treasurer, Due Dates and Penalties. The county accepts a mailed payment as on time when the postmark is on or before the due date, and all personal property tax is payable in full by May 15.

sections.h2: What does a late payment cost in Isanti County?
sections.html:
Miss a due date and Minnesota law adds a percentage penalty that grows each month. Under Minnesota Statutes section 279.01, the first penalty is 2% on homestead property and 4% on nonhomestead property.

If the installment is still open on the first day of the next month, the same percentage is added again. From then until December, one more percent is added on the first of each month. The total stops at 8% for a homestead and 12% for a nonhomestead parcel. A rental house or a vacant inherited home usually falls in the higher group, so an estate holding an Isanti County house that has been left unpaid for a few months can see a double-digit penalty.

The statute also says the treasurer must forgive the penalty once if a payment is mailed and postmarked within one business day of the due date, provided the owner has not used that relief before.

sections.h2: How do I appeal my Isanti County valuation?
sections.html:
Start with the assessor, then the local board of appeal and equalization in your city or township, then the county board. Court is the last step.

For a court challenge, Minnesota Statutes section 278.01 gives two doors. A petition to district court has to be served on the county auditor and filed with the court administrator by April 30 of the year the tax is payable. A Tax Court appeal can be started after the valuation notice arrives and before May 1 of that year. The county's local board page shows meeting dates on its calendar, and the November 2026 calendar lists no meetings, so check back in the spring after notices are mailed.

Appealing does not excuse payment. Section 279.01 says the treasurer may take partial payments and that doing so does not waive the minimum payment required to keep an appeal alive under section 278.03. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer what that minimum is before you file.

sections.h2: Which Isanti County application dates matter to a homeowner?
sections.html:
The assessor's application calendar runs on the assessment year, and an application filed late usually takes effect a year later. The county lists these cutoffs:

  • Homestead, and actively farming or special agricultural homestead: December 31.
  • Blind or disabled special homestead: October 1.
  • Mobile home homesteads: May 31.
  • Green Acres, Rural Preserve, managed forest land and nonprofit community service organizations: May 1.
  • Exempt properties: July 1. Sustainable forest: September 30.

Source: Isanti County Application Deadlines. Agricultural use must be in place by January 2 of the assessment year to apply to the following payable year.

Separately, the Minnesota Department of Revenue says the Homestead Credit Refund is due August 15 and can be claimed for up to one year after that date.

sections.h2: How are taxes handled when I sell an Isanti County house?
sections.html:
The tax bill stays with the parcel, so unpaid tax has to be settled at or before closing. Ask the Isanti County Auditor-Treasurer for the amount due on your parcel number, including any penalty and any special assessment.

If a lender escrows your taxes, the lender pays on your behalf and the statement will say not to pay it yourself. When you sell, the purchase contract decides how the current year is split between buyer and seller. Bring the most recent statement and the closing date to the treasurer's office so the payoff matches what the title company will request.

faqs.q: What is the second half deadline for a regular Isanti County home?
faqs.a: October 15 for a residential property. The county lists agricultural and manufactured home second halves on November 15, and a mailed payment counts as on time if postmarked by the due date.

faqs.q: Where is the Isanti County Assessor located?
faqs.a: The Assessor accepts applications by mail at 555 18th Avenue SW, Cambridge, Minnesota 55008. Cambridge is also the county seat.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Isanti County value after the spring meetings?
faqs.a: Yes, through court. A district court petition must be filed by April 30 of the payable year, and a Tax Court appeal can start after the valuation notice arrives and before May 1, under Minnesota Statutes section 278.01.

faqs.q: How much is the late penalty on an Isanti County rental house?
faqs.a: It starts at 4% on a nonhomestead parcel and can reach 12% by December, under section 279.01. A homestead starts at 2% and tops out at 8%.

faqs.q: When should I file for homestead in Isanti County?
faqs.a: By December 31 of the assessment year for it to apply to taxes payable the next year. Blind or disabled special homestead has an October 1 cutoff.
